A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PatchAlign3D. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison. Internal inconsistencies in new results do not prevent identifying the revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments, training and encoder ablations, and zero-shot and few-shot KeypointNet results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds patch-granularity, boundary, prompt-sensitivity, negative-sampling, and ZeroKey-integration experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds a hybrid inference procedure that modulates ZeroKey soft-voting scores using patch–text similarities and injects local features into clustering. The original PatchAlign3D architecture, two-stage training, and segmentation inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training corpus, five segmentation benchmarks, and KeypointNet task are retained. Table 11 adds inference scenarios using category-enriched queries and difficult synonyms, extending the tested textual input conditions without adding datasets.

E2.justification: New Table 14 evaluates ZeroKey and StablePoints alongside PatchAlign3D and previously evaluated methods. ZeroKey was previously cited for the evaluation protocol but was absent from the reported comparator rows. Existing segmentation and keypoint comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New appendix experiments vary patch size and count at fixed input size, evaluate boundary mIoU on mixed-label 16-neighbor regions, hold the model fixed across prompt variants, and test additional cross-shape negatives. Previously stated splits, default model settings, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A substantially expands direct testing of central design choices: patch granularity versus localization, boundary accuracy, prompt robustness, and within-shape versus cross-shape negatives. Appendix C additionally tests whether the features benefit ZeroKey. These analyses supplement the retained stage, encoder, and freezing ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new prompt experiment's fixed trained model is an experimental control, not an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–9 and the keypoint results in v1 Table 10, now v2 Table 13, retain their values. New Tables 10–12 and 14 add substantial results, including 56.9 versus 45.3 mIoU for within-shape versus additional cross-shape negatives. Table 14 reports hybrid gains at its medium and large thresholds but a decline from 13.16 to 10.42 at the smallest. Inconsistent labels prevent interpreting its reused older scores as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation (4) changes the patch–text score from using z_i directly to using h_text(z_i), explicitly including the already-described projection head. This corrects the mathematical score definition without establishing a new core architecture. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: language-aligned patch features, two-stage pre-training, and efficient zero-shot segmentation outperforming prior approaches. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning the trade-off between patch context and boundary precision, generalization across query wording, and complementary geometric cues for ZeroKey. The original annotation-noise rationale and limitations concerning training coverage and fixed patching remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies exact patch configurations, the 16-neighbor boundary-selection criterion, fixed-model prompt controls, and the insertion points for ZeroKey integration. Captions also explicitly identify ShapeNetPart for retained ablations. Existing training details and project access information are unchanged; detailed hybrid implementation settings remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The bibliography and main related-work discussion are retained. Appendix C newly positions PatchAlign3D as complementary to ZeroKey through an integrated method, extending the earlier relationship in which Gong et al. supplied the keypoint evaluation protocol.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain stable. V2 expands the appendix overview, adds analysis paragraphs, clarifies inference in Figure 2's caption, and makes small wording and header edits, including removing the contact email and supplementary title block.

P2.justification: V2 adds four appendix tables, reformats Figure 1, updates several captions, and rearranges retained appendix displays. The original keypoint table is renumbered from 10 to 13. Most existing figures and table structures remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful direct tests of design choices that v1 lacked, but introduces reporting conflicts. Table 11 gives the baseline mIoU/cIoU as 53.1/56.9, reversing the retained 56.9/53.1. Table 14 repeats earlier few-shot values under different threshold labels and drops the few-shot designation; for example, 7.80 moves from threshold 0.001 to 0.01. These unresolved inconsistencies weaken interpretation of the added evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
